title: Effect of sports massage on performance and recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
claims: The review identified 29 eligible randomised studies recruiting 1,012 participants.
There was no evidence that massage improves measures of strength, jump, sprint, endurance or fatigue.
Massage was associated with small but statistically significant improvements in flexibility and delayed-onset muscle soreness.
DOMS improved by approximately 13%, with SMD 1.13 (95% CI 0.44 to 1.82; 311 participants; 10 studies; I² = 86%).
Sports massage is defined in the review as manual manipulation of muscles and soft tissue by a qualified professional, with the purpose of improving performance in or recovery from sport.
